newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks post biggest gain ever.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks post biggest gain ever.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index ended a week of constant retreat with another heavy fall, tumbling below the 4,600 level in late trade as index futures dived. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,593.9, down 59.8 points, or 1.29 percent. This was 189.2 points down from last Friday.

FRANKFURT - Stocks raced to early gains in bourse dealings and held on to most of the advance in moderate activity tied to the "triple witching" expiry of DAX futures, DAX options and stock options. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,788.27, up 39.00 points, or 1.04 percent, a rise of 43.83 on the week. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,788.54, up 10.98 points, or 0.29 percent.

PARIS - Stocks rose sharply as investors gave the new Socialist-led government the benefit of the doubt after what was viewed as a prudent keynote policy speech by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Thursday. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,757.10, up 17.41 points, or 0.64 percent, a fall of 51.42 from last week.

ZURICH - Shares closed at a third straight record high in both the blue-chip and broad indexes as gains in several high-profile stocks propelled the market. The Swiss market index closed at 5,561.8, up 51.5 points, or 0.93 percent and up 177.2 on the week.

TOKYO - Stocks ended lower as investors squared positions ahead of the weekend and the G7 summit due to start later in the day. They said the scandal involving Japanese brokers and racketeers also hurt the market, pressuring brokerage shares. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,385.54, down 122.31 points, or 0.60 percent. This was down 142.81 from last Friday.

HONG KONG - Stocks staged their biggest point gain ever, forging into record ground on a wave of euphoria ahead of the handover of the British colony to China. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,154.36, up 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, for a rise of 1,041.81 points on the week.

SYDNEY - A wave of confidence from overseas investors in Australia's resource and banking sectors carried local stocks to both a record close. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,712.6, up 19.3 points, or 0.72 percent, a rise of 57.30 from the previous Friday's close.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial shares ended firmly higerr on positive underlying sentiment. The All-share index closed at 7,234.1, up 25.0 points, or 0.35 percent, down 37.4 from a week ago. The All Gold index closed at 1,027.4, down 33.9 points, or 0.92 percent, a drop of 101.6 since last week, while the Industrial index closed at 8,511.5, up 77.7 points, or 3.19 percent. This was up 29.1 from last Friday.
